title: FizzBuzz
prompt: A classroom game counts from 1 to n with special words for certain numbers. Write a function that returns an array where multiples of 3 become "Fizz", multiples of 5 become "Buzz", multiples of both become "FizzBuzz", and every other number becomes its own string.

explanation.beginner:
Example: fizzbuzz(5) produces ["1","2","Fizz","4","Buzz"]. The result must follow this precise rule: A classroom game counts from 1 to n with special words for certain numbers. Write a function that returns an array where multiples of 3 become "Fizz", multiples of 5 become "Buzz", multiples of both become "FizzBuzz", and every other number becomes its own string. Work with one argument at a time and distinguish the values that select a branch from the values returned by that branch.

Compare “marks FizzBuzz at 15”: input [15] produces ["1","2","Fizz","4","Buzz","Fizz","7","8","Fizz","Buzz","11","Fizz","13","14","FizzBuzz"]. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
